root_cause: Votes had no ordering key: the live handleVote and castVote upserted by arrival, the early-vote replay alone compared sender created_at, and the early-vote queue kept the latest arrival. Delivery order, a journal replay after a failed ack, or clock skew between a voter's devices therefore decided which vote a member kept, so members could diverge. Separately, handleClose (and the chatHandler poll_close announcement gate) dropped a close whose poll was not yet known, so under MLS reordering the poll stayed open forever on that member.
fix: Implemented the adopted design (bug-reports/poll-ordering-design-2026-10-15.md). §1: PollVotePayload.seq (optional non-negative safe integer, parsePollVote rejects anything else); isNewerVote total order (seq, created_at, rumorId), legacy = seq 0 / ''. §2: saveVote replaced by saveVoteIfNewer, a compare-and-set inside pollPersistence's per-key enqueue used by handleVote, replayPendingVotes (votedAt skip removed), castVote and thereby journal replay; queuePendingVote keeps the newer entry; new pollCast.ts (createVoteCaster/nextVoteSeq) derives seq = max(stored own, own queued, 0)+1 with per-(group,poll) serialisation, stores the sent rumor's created_at/id, and PollStoreContext's optimistic setVotes applies the comparator. §3: persisted bounded pending-close queue (few:poll-pending-closes:{groupId}, <=10 polls per sender per group, <=50 per group oldest evicted, 7-day TTL) applied in handleOpen's new-poll path after the vote replay only when closer == authenticated creator (case-insensitive), else discarded; the chatHandler poll_close gate now queues an announcement for an unknown poll (few:poll-pending-close-announcements:{groupId}, same bounds) and createPollCloseAnnouncementReplayer re-runs it through the same handle()/gate after the open (wired via pollHandler onPollOpened in registerHandlers); a getPoll throw still rejects without queueing. clearPollData/clearAllPollData clear both new queues. AC-9 amended, docs/behavior/polls.md updated, pollReplay.ts doc comment rewritten.
deviations_from_design: Pending-close and pending-announcement entries are unique per (group, poll, SENDER), first kept, instead of per (group, poll): with one slot per poll, any member who learned a fresh poll id could pre-empt the slot with a forged close that is later discarded, and the creator's genuine close (arriving second) would have been dropped. All other bounds are as designed; the AC-9 text says 'one entry per poll and sender'.

The chatHandler gate consistency (design: 'queue/re-evaluate consistently') is realised as a second queue holding only the announcement rumor's identity (id, sender, created_at); on the open it is re-run through the unchanged chat handle() path, so the row appears with the recomputed tally, at its original timestamp, and counts as unread at that moment.

verification_answers.VQ-1: Yes. pollPersistence.saveVoteIfNewer is the only vote write (saveVote removed); it reads, compares with isNewerVote and writes inside enqueue(votesKey). handleVote, replayPendingVotes, castVote (pollCast) and journal replay (which re-dispatches through handleVote) all call it. Evidence: pollOrdering 'keeps the greatest vote for every call order, also when the calls race' (6 orders via Promise.all).
verification_answers.VQ-2: Yes. pollOrdering 'two devices of one user with clock skew' covers A,B; B,A; both queued then open (both orders); queued+live (both orders); journal replay re-delivering A after B; stranded replay; closed tally — all converge on B. The equivalent throwaway repro against HEAD code failed (stored A).
verification_answers.VQ-3: Yes. nextVoteSeq = max(own stored seq, own queued seq, 0)+1 (case-insensitive own match); createVoteCaster chains casts per group:poll. Tests: stored 3 + queued 5 -> 6; two rapid casts -> 6, 7; failed send consumes nothing. isNewerVote treats absent seq as 0; tests 'seq >= 1 beats a legacy vote', 'legacy vote arriving after a seq vote is ignored', 'stored legacy row replaced by any seq>=1 vote'.
verification_answers.VQ-4: Yes. parsePollVote rejects present seq that is negative, fractional, string, null, boolean, object or > MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (it.each). handleClose queues an unknown-poll close with the authenticated closer; handleOpen applies it only when closer equals the authenticated creator (case-insensitive), else removes it (tests: non-creator discarded, attacker-first cannot crowd out, cross-group). Bounds: <=10 per sender, <=50 per group oldest-by-receipt evicted, 7-day TTL incl. boundary, persisted across reload. Deviation: unique per (poll, sender) instead of per poll — see deviations_from_design.
verification_answers.VQ-5: Yes. The chatHandler poll_close gate queues (not drops) an announcement for an unknown poll and re-runs it through the same gate after the open (createPollCloseAnnouncementReplayer via onPollOpened); lookup failures still reject. AC-9 has both designed sentences (queue wording 'one entry per poll and sender'); docs/behavior/polls.md replaces the arrival-order text (§3, §7, §8, Sources); pollReplay.ts comment replaced with the CAS/order-insensitive explanation.
verification_answers.VQ-6: Yes. Unit 5193 passed / 1 skipped (245 files), tsc clean. Stryker concurrency 1: no real-gap survivors after round 2 (91.62%). Poll e2e 42/42 and full gate (72 + 345 passed, 19 skipped) green.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The design's 'one pending close per (group, poll), first kept' let a forged early close pre-empt the creator's, and its chatHandler item ('queue/re-evaluate consistently') named the goal but not the mechanism, so both needed implementation-time decisions that are recorded as deviations rather than settled in the design.
retrospective.surprised_by: pgrep -f in a Monitor until-loop matches the monitor's own command line, so a 'wait until process gone' monitor never fires; the background task's own completion notice is the reliable signal.

remediation_round_1.fix: pollHandler.ts: extracted settleHeldCloses (apply the creator held close if the poll is still open: loadVotesWithPending -> computeTally -> savePoll closed, all BEFORE removing held entries; discard non-creator entries; then replay held announcements best-effort) + best-effort recoverHeldCloses. Called on the open new-poll path (after replayPendingVotes, still throwing as before), the open existing-poll branch, handleVote (also for an already-closed poll, announcements only; a vote arriving after a recovered close is dropped) and handleClose known-poll path (also for a non-creator close). A close of an already-closed poll is now a no-op (closing is final; previously recomputed the same tally). UI bumped once when recovery closes the poll. Misleading comment replaced. Dep onPollOpened renamed replayHeldCloseAnnouncements (no longer open-only). docs/behavior/polls.md §7 states the retry.
